question: A 15-metre error in Earth's position grows tenfold every 10 million years. How large after 100 million years, in millions of km?
answer: 150 million km: about the distance from Earth to the Sun.
move: An error that multiplies will outrun any error that merely adds.
trap: Guessing a few kilometres, as if the error grew by steady additions.
hint: Count how many tenfold steps fit into the time, then multiply.
steps: 100 million years is 10 periods of 10 million years.
Ten tenfold growths multiply the error by 10,000,000,000.
150 million km: about the distance from Earth to the Sun.

diagram.caption: Tenfold every 10 million years turns 15 metres into the distance to the Sun.

source: Laskar, Is the Solar System Stable?, 2013
